question.text: Which of the following is NOT a member of the panel constituted by the stock exchange for compulsory delisting under SEBI Delisting Regulations, 2021?

answer.text: Two directors of the stock exchange (one being a public representative)
A representative of an investor association recognized by SEBI
A representative of the Reserve Bank of India
An Executive Director or Secretary of the stock exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: The compulsory delisting panel constituted by the stock exchange consists of two directors of the stock exchange (one being a public representative), one representative of an investor association recognized by SEBI, one representative of the MCA/Registrar of Companies, and the Executive Director or Secretary of the stock exchange. A representative of the RBI is not a member of this panel. The Trap: Because RBI is a major financial regulator, it is tempting to assume it sits on every SEBI-related panel. The compulsory delisting panel is focused on stock exchange, investor protection, and corporate compliance representation, so RBI is the correct "NOT a member" choice. Note: The composition of the compulsory delisting panel is set out in the SEBI Delisting Regulations, 2021. Avoid citing a "Chartered Accountant" as a panel member, since that is not in the workbook-supported composition.
